description: I'm Trisha and I'm interested in new things
summary:
Astro Kids developed Moonbase Commander, an interactive Scratch game that puts young players in charge of a lunar outpost. Their mission is to keep four astronauts safe and healthy until the next supply ship arrives. Across three increasingly long missions, players manage oxygen, water, food, and power while deciding how to spend a limited budget on equipment like solar panels, batteries, and radiation shielding.

The game addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by letting players see how one decision affects the rest of the base. Pausing the greenhouse lights can save power, but it also slows food production. Buying more batteries can help the crew get through periods of low sunlight, but it leaves less money for other upgrades. By testing different strategies and seeing the consequences, players learn how engineers balance competing needs to keep a real space mission running.
details:
How it works

In Moonbase Commander, you’re in charge of a Moon base. Your job is to keep four astronauts safe and healthy until their supplies arrive. There are three missions that last 3, 5, and 8 days. Each turn, you check the forecast, review your supplies, and decide whether to buy equipment or save your coins before choosing Next Day. When you win, your leftover coins and mission reward carry over to the next base.

What players learn

We wanted young players to see how one decision can affect the whole base. A greenhouse grows food, but it also uses power and water. You can switch off its lights to save both, but then the greenhouse stops producing food. Solar panels generate power in sunlight, batteries store power for shadow days, and a storm shelter protects the crew from radiation. Players can retry a mission to see how a different plan changes the outcome.

How we made it

Astro Kids came up with the mission, the four-person crew, and the ideas for longer missions, base upgrades, and a budget that carries over. OpenAI Codex helped turn those ideas into a working game using Scratch blocks. We used TurboWarp to package it for web browsers and a NASA Apollo 15 photo for the lunar backdrop. The resource amounts and mission lengths are simplified so first-time players can focus on the choices and see their effects after each turn.
